exposure: immigrant status/origin (sub-Saharan, Latin America, Eastern Europe, Maghreb)
outcome: Apgar score in the first minute < 7
cohort: The study included 17,281 pregnant women in the Lleida health region of Spain who gave birth between 2012 and 2018.
finding: Immigrant populations in Spain show varying risks for adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes compared to native-born women, with some immigrant groups (e.g., sub-Saharan) experiencing higher rates of preeclampsia, C-sections, and lower Apgar scores.
mod_finding: Sub-Saharan and Latin American women had a higher percentage of cesarean sections, while women from Eastern Europe and the Maghreb population had a lower percentage compared to the overall average.
